indexPrompt.rag-answer-in-a-long-chunk: An answer sentence sits inside a chunk of m related sentences, scored as the mean of their vectors. Find the chunk's cosine similarity with the question, the largest m for which it still beats an unrelated one-sentence warning, and where that cosine tends as m grows.
indexPrompt.rag-same-budget-smaller-chunks: A retriever is tested over a camera manual chunked two ways, into 400-token chunks and 200-token chunks, with room for 800 tokens of retrieved text. Ten test questions give the rank of the answer chunk under each chunking. Which chunk size should the team use, and on what evidence?
indexPrompt.rag-chance-cosines: Model a note that has nothing to do with the question as a random direction in 400 dimensions, and work out the standard deviation of its cosine similarity with the question, then how many of 100,000 unrelated notes are expected to outrank an answer note.
indexPrompt.rag-idf-after-new-notes: Two notes keep their words and the question keeps its words, but the collection grows from 6 notes to 12. Recompute the idf weights and both cosine similarities, and explain why the ranking flips.
indexPrompt.rag-overlapping-windows: A manual is chunked into windows of 6 sentences with a stride t between starts. Find the probability that a 3-sentence answer stays whole inside one chunk, the smallest overlap that always keeps it whole, and what that overlap costs.
indexPrompt.rag-weighting-two-scores: A help desk mixes a dense cosine similarity and a TF-IDF cosine similarity into one score with a weight alpha. For each of two questions, find the range of alpha that puts the answer note first, and choose one alpha for both.
